record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.context_brief: Hybrid evolutionary and mathematical programming methods
record.original_question: How can evolutionary algorithms be effectively hybridized with mathematical programming techniques, including game-theoretic methods, min-max optimality, or epsilon-constraint-style methods, to produce stronger multi-objective evolutionary algorithms?

evidence.quote: underestimated the potential of hybridizing evolutionary algorithms with mathematical programming techniques.
game theory, min-max optimality, and the ε-constraint method

artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to hybridize evolutionary algorithms with mathematical programming techniques (ε-constraint, min-max scalarization, game-theoretic methods) to produce provably stronger multiobjective evolutionary algorithms remains an active and open research direction. While many heuristic memetic and hybrid MOEA schemes have been proposed, no general theory establishing strict improvement guarantees under broad assumptions is known.

status_evidence.title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists hybridization of evolutionary algorithms with mathematical programming techniques among the open problems in evolutionary multiobjective optimization.
status_evidence.claim: The hybridization question is explicitly listed as an open problem.
